title: Add automated lint checks and provenance tags for legacy chart instances
creator: Maya Chen
description: Many of our chart components in the Figma library originate from ad-hoc redesigns and contain outdated tokens, forced overrides, and broken auto-layout that bypass the token system. This ticket adds persistent provenance metadata to instances and implements an automated linting rule set that runs during library pre-publish to detect and classify legacy issues. The goal is to reduce regressions pushed by stale instances, make ownership visible, and enable bulk remediation through a guided batch-fix flow.
background: During the last library audit we found ~120 chart instances with mixed token usage, missing semantic tokens, and manual layer renames. These cause visual drift in downstream apps and make rollouts fragile. Currently authorship and modification history is hard to attribute; we need lightweight provenance tags and a lint pipeline to prevent regressions at publish time.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance tag added to each library component and instance; tag includes author, last_modified_date, and 'legacy' flag when token mismatches are detected.
A set of lint rules implemented as a JS/Node Figma plugin or CI script that flags: deprecated tokens, hard-coded color/spacing, auto-layout violations, and renamed semantic layers.
Pre-publish hook integrated: publish is blocked (with override) if >5 high severity lint findings exist.
Batch-fix guide and helper scripts created for common issues (replace deprecated tokens, restore auto-layout constraints).
Dashboard (sheet) summarizing lint findings per component and owner for at least one weekly run.
tasks: Draft lint rule list and severity matrix (Maya)
Prototype provenance tag schema and small Figma plugin (Arjun)
Run an audit pass on 'Charts' and 'Tables' pages and capture findings (Maya)
Implement pre-publish CI hook that calls lint runner (Engowner: ENG-2147)
Create batch-fix scripts for token replacement and auto-layout restoration
Write design doc and publish remediation playbook for design engineers
Schedule a walkthrough with platform and docs to align on publisher UX
comments: 2025-11-03 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after audit; initial scope limited to charts and table primitives to keep rollout small.

2025-11-07 - Arjun Patel: Spike complete. Prototype plugin can inject a hidden description node with provenance JSON (author,lastModifiedIso,legacyReason). Works in latest Figma desktop only; web requires CORS workaround.
2025-11-10 - Maya Chen: Decided to classify lint severities as low/medium/high. High = missing semantic tokens or broken auto-layout, medium = deprecated token usage, low = naming inconsistencies.
2025-11-13 - Arjun Patel: Built initial lint runner. Found 137 instances with at least one high severity issue across 6 chart components. Exported CSV and linked to remediation sheet.
2025-11-15 - Maya Chen: Design review: agreed to add a visible owner annotation in component description and include 'migration_level' tag (auto, manual-required).

2025-11-18 - Arjun Patel: Implemented pre-publish check as a lightweight GitHub Action that calls the lint runner via figma-rest API token. Action blocks publish PRs when >5 high issues unless 'force-publish' label is present.

2025-11-20 - Maya Chen: QA pass on batch-fix script successful for 28 instances (token replacement). Auto-layout fixes still require manual validation in some nested cases. Moving to in-review for docs and rollout plan.
